story.value: Fermium was discovered in 1952 by a team of scientists led by Albert Ghiorso.
Fermium is named after the Italian physicist and Nobel Laureate Enrico Fermi.
The Berkeley team named the element in honor of Enrico Fermi, the developer of the first artificial self-sustained nuclear reactor.

uses.value: Because only small amounts are produced and its half-life is short, fermium currently has no uses outside of basic scientific research.
Fermium is currently used only in basic scientific research that expands knowledge of the rest of the periodic table.
